title: Go command and argument boundaries
prompt_hint: Distinguish os/exec argv from sh -c; fixed executables can still interpret attacker-controlled flags.
review_checks: Resolve the imported API and identify which actor controls the executable, arguments and environment.
Check shell interpretation and command-specific option injection separately; constructing Cmd does not establish that Run/Start/Output is called.
remediation: Prefer a fixed executable and separate validated arguments; apply command-specific option and working-directory restrictions.
benign_considerations: A fixed command with purpose-bound arguments is a capability, not evidence of hostile execution.

examples.scenario: A skill inserts a downloaded task string into a shell command and starts it.
A task invokes a fixed formatter on validated workspace paths using an argument array.

title: Go credential-to-request evidence
prompt_hint: Trace sensitive reads into URL, headers or body; NewRequest constructs a request and does not itself transmit it.
review_checks: Identify the actual sensitive source, transformations and destination field, including URL/query/header/body.
Require a visible send operation before asserting transmission; missing callees or recipients remain unknown.
remediation: Limit data to the task and intended recipient; keep secrets out of URLs and diagnostic output.
benign_considerations: Sending a scoped token to its intended authentication endpoint can be legitimate.

examples.scenario: A helper collects all environment variables and posts them to an unrelated diagnostic collector.
A client attaches one service token to an authorized request for that service.

title: Go URL and redirect controls
prompt_hint: For attacker-selected URLs inspect parsing, redirects and resolved destinations; URL concatenation is not a host allowlist.
review_checks: Locate URL input and the request operation; distinguish fixed authorized endpoints from attacker selection.
Check redirects and private/reserved destinations at the connection boundary; source alone may not establish DNS/runtime enforcement.
remediation: Choose destinations from an approved set or enforce URL, resolution, redirect and egress controls.
benign_considerations: A declared local-service client can intentionally contact loopback; task authorization and deployment matter.

examples.scenario: A public tool fetches a supplied URL with ambient cloud credentials and unrestricted redirects.
A service selects one fixed documented endpoint from a small configuration map.

title: Go filesystem and archive containment
prompt_hint: Cleaning a path is not containment; inspect absolute paths, parent traversal, symlinks and archive entry writes.
review_checks: Trace untrusted filenames or archive member names to a filesystem operation and its intended root.
Check containment and link handling at the actual write/open boundary; string-prefix checks alone are insufficient.
remediation: Use root-confined filesystem operations and reject escaping archive paths, links and unsupported entry types.
benign_considerations: Opening a user-selected file outside a workspace can be intentional when specifically authorized.

examples.scenario: An installer joins archive member names to its target and overwrites files outside that directory.
An extractor confines writes to its destination and rejects escaping or unsupported entries.

title: Go query construction and parameters
prompt_hint: Follow external data to executed SQL; database placeholders bind values, not arbitrary table names or syntax.
review_checks: Distinguish query text construction from an actual Query/Exec sink.
Check value parameter binding and allowlisted dynamic identifiers independently.
remediation: Bind values with the database driver and choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist.
benign_considerations: A fully constant query or a composed query with only validated fixed identifiers is not automatically injectable.

examples.scenario: A tool concatenates a request-supplied filter into a database command.
A query keeps user values in driver-bound parameters.

title: Go TLS validation and effective configuration
prompt_hint: Evaluate the effective TLS configuration and verification callbacks; a protocol constant or TLS import is not a bypass.
review_checks: Find disabled certificate/hostname verification and determine whether a real verification callback replaces it.
Check the configuration actually reaches the client transport; distinguish minimum protocol selection from validation bypass.
remediation: Keep identity verification enabled and configure supported protocol floors for the deployed environment.
benign_considerations: A test-only TLS setting is contextual evidence, not a blanket exemption for production paths.

examples.scenario: A distributed skill disables verification on the transport used to upload workspace data.
A client uses normal trust validation with an explicitly configured modern minimum protocol.

title: JavaScript and TypeScript process APIs
prompt_hint: Differentiate exec shell strings from execFile/spawn argv; shell:true and downstream interpreters restore shell risk.
review_checks: Follow untrusted input into executable, argument, shell option, cwd and environment positions.
Resolve aliases and wrappers only when supported by supplied evidence; TypeScript annotations do not validate runtime input.
remediation: Use a fixed executable with validated argv and explicit shell settings; restrict interpreted flags.
benign_considerations: A legitimate build command may require execution; the command and authorization determine the concern.

examples.scenario: An extension concatenates a repository title into child_process.exec.
An extension calls an approved executable with validated individual arguments and no shell.

title: JavaScript dynamic evaluation and vm boundaries
prompt_hint: Track input to eval, Function, templates or vm; a new vm context alone is not an isolation guarantee.
review_checks: Identify who controls evaluated text and whether host objects or privileged functions are exposed.
Distinguish parsing inert data from evaluating expressions and distinguish context separation from OS isolation.
remediation: Keep inputs as data; use an appropriate isolated execution environment for deliberately untrusted programs.
benign_considerations: Parsing a bounded JSON document does not itself evaluate JavaScript.

examples.scenario: A plugin evaluates a server response while exposing process and filesystem objects.
A plugin parses a schema-validated JSON response and dispatches a fixed operation.

title: Node environment and file disclosure
prompt_hint: Trace process.env and file reads into fetch/http, logs or subprocess environments; collection alone is not transmission.
review_checks: Identify which values can be sensitive and whether the recipient and purpose are authorized.
Inspect serialization, request bodies, query strings, headers and logging; distinguish object construction from a network send.
remediation: Select only required fields and prevent credentials or private files entering unrelated requests and logs.
benign_considerations: Reading a named environment variable for its intended service can be normal authentication.

examples.scenario: A bootstrap script serializes process.env into an unrelated telemetry request.
A tool sends only the requested public search query to its documented provider.

title: Prototype mutation through dynamic keys
prompt_hint: Dynamic keys become a concern when they reach shared prototypes or security-relevant configuration; key strings alone are insufficient.
review_checks: Trace attacker-controlled property paths through assignments or merges to shared objects.
Check prototype-free dictionaries, own-property checks and explicit key schemas along the actual path.
remediation: Use Map or an appropriate prototype-free structure and validate allowed property paths.
benign_considerations: A Map entry containing a special-looking string does not mutate Object.prototype.

examples.scenario: An untrusted settings object is recursively merged into process-wide authorization defaults.
A parser stores validated independent entries in Map without modifying shared prototypes.

title: Node request target and browser automation scope
prompt_hint: Inspect attacker-selected request targets and redirects; being a browser or fetch wrapper does not establish an egress boundary.
review_checks: Identify whether user or tool-result data controls the URL, proxy or request headers.
Check destination enforcement and redirects, and whether ambient credentials accompany requests.
remediation: Constrain destinations and credential forwarding at the actual request boundary.
benign_considerations: A user-authorized URL fetch is expected behavior; restrictions depend on deployment and accessible networks.

examples.scenario: A remote renderer accepts arbitrary URLs while forwarding a workspace bearer token.
A client selects a known destination and sends only credentials intended for it.

title: npm lifecycle and package source changes
prompt_hint: Lifecycle scripts and dependency source overrides may execute or select code during install; declaration is not observed execution.
review_checks: Inspect preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare scripts, git or URL dependencies and registry overrides.
Determine which package manager and install mode would actually activate the declaration; inspect referenced local scripts.
remediation: Review install-time code and dependency sources; prefer reviewed immutable inputs with explicit update review.
benign_considerations: A documented native compilation step may be a legitimate lifecycle operation.

examples.scenario: An otherwise unrelated helper package runs an opaque downloaded script during installation.
A package builds a reviewed local native component through a documented lifecycle script.

title: Generated text entering active contexts
prompt_hint: Treat model or tool output as data when it enters HTML, templates, SQL or execution; escaping must match the receiving context.
review_checks: Find the generated value and the interpreter or active rendering sink.
Check context-appropriate encoding or structured APIs; validation for one context does not cover another.
remediation: Use inert rendering and structured parameter APIs rather than building active templates or commands.
benign_considerations: Rendering text through an escaping API is different from executing a constructed template.

examples.scenario: A tool response is appended to a template source and evaluated on the server.
A fixed template receives an untrusted value only as escaped display data.

title: Python subprocess interpretation
prompt_hint: Check shell=True, os.system and argument provenance; shell=False prevents shell parsing but not unsafe program options.
review_checks: Resolve the actual call and shell value, including aliases and wrappers visible in the excerpt.
Distinguish fixed argv, attacker-selected executables and command-specific options; an unevaluated call is not proof of execution.
remediation: Use a fixed executable, validated argument lists and appropriate option boundaries.
benign_considerations: A documented task-specific subprocess call is not inherently malicious.

examples.scenario: A skill uses shell=True to execute a command built from an external task description.
A skill runs an approved local checker with a validated argv list.

title: Python evaluation, imports and decoding chains
prompt_hint: Track untrusted bytes through decode/compile/eval/exec/import; removing builtins is not a secure sandbox.
review_checks: Identify the original input and each necessary transformation into an execution-capable operation.
Distinguish inspection or decoding from subsequent evaluation; unknown imports and callees remain unknown.
remediation: Use inert data formats and fixed dispatch; isolate execution when it is a deliberate product requirement.
benign_considerations: Base64 used for an image or decoding text without executing it is not an execution chain.

examples.scenario: A plugin decodes a network response and executes it in the host process.
A decoder validates image data and writes it to a bounded media output.

title: Python object construction from untrusted data
prompt_hint: Check input trust and exact loader options for pickle, object-capable YAML and related loaders; load-like names are not enough.
review_checks: Resolve the loader and configuration; distinguish safe-data loaders from object reconstruction.
Follow file/network input to the deserializer and identify who can replace the serialized bytes.
remediation: Use a bounded data-only format and schema; do not treat a filename, extension or self-declared signature as trusted origin.
benign_considerations: A safe YAML loader does not acquire object-construction behavior merely because its name includes load.

examples.scenario: A skill unpickles an attachment received from an unauthenticated endpoint.
A skill parses bounded configuration with a data-only loader and validates the schema.

title: Python environment, files and network flows
prompt_hint: Trace os.environ or file reads to network arguments, headers and logs; a variable named token is not proof of a secret.
review_checks: Identify actual source sensitivity, requested purpose and final recipient.
Review visible aliases, wrappers and serialization without inventing cross-file flow.
remediation: Read and disclose the minimum data required for the explicitly authorized task.
benign_considerations: Purpose-bound credential exchange and writing local diagnostic metadata may be legitimate.

examples.scenario: A plugin uploads a credentials file as an undocumented diagnostic attachment.
A client reads one scoped token to authenticate to its intended service.

title: Python path and archive extraction controls
prompt_hint: Inspect containment, symlink/special-file handling and effective tar filters; Python version and extraction options matter.
review_checks: Trace untrusted archive member names or path input to the final write/open operation.
Inspect explicit extraction filters and runtime defaults; do not infer that every extractall call is unsafe.
remediation: Confine extraction to an approved root, apply an appropriate filter and bound entry counts and expanded size.
benign_considerations: A properly restricted extraction can be legitimate; the local runtime version may be unknown.

examples.scenario: A package installer extracts untrusted archive paths over unrelated user configuration.
An extractor enforces root containment, restricted types, filtering and resource bounds.

title: Python SQL text versus bound values
prompt_hint: Check formatted SQL reaching execute/executemany; a string resembling SQL without an execution sink is weaker evidence.
review_checks: Identify external data in the query text and the database execution API.
Check parameter binding separately from formatting and allowlist any dynamic identifiers.
remediation: Use driver-supported placeholders for values and fixed mappings for SQL identifiers.
benign_considerations: A parameterized query or a standalone SQL documentation example does not establish injection.

examples.scenario: A skill uses a user-supplied project name inside the executed SQL text.
A query supplies the project name through the driver parameter mechanism.

title: Shell download-to-execution chains
prompt_hint: Trace curl/wget bytes through pipes, temporary files and substitutions into shell input; downloading alone is not execution.
review_checks: Identify the source and each visible flow into a shell or executable file.
Check content verification against a separately trusted expected digest or signer; fetching a checksum beside a payload does not independently authenticate it.
remediation: Review and authenticate executable bytes before running them and avoid hidden install-time execution.
benign_considerations: Downloading a data artifact for an authorized task without executing it is different from remote execution.

examples.scenario: An installer pipes an unreviewed network response directly into a privileged shell.
A tool downloads a data file, checks the separately supplied expected digest and parses it as data.

title: Shell eval, source and interpreter re-entry
prompt_hint: eval, source/dot and sh -c re-enter execution; quoting at an earlier stage does not make later evaluation inert.
review_checks: Trace the origin of evaluated text or sourced filenames, including downloaded and workspace-controlled files.
Inspect actual execution semantics; printing or discussing an eval command is not invoking it.
remediation: Use fixed commands and argument arrays; source only explicitly trusted and reviewed configuration code.
benign_considerations: A sourced reviewed environment setup can be expected; the file path alone does not establish trust.

examples.scenario: A helper reads a task response and passes it to eval.
A script parses a task identifier and chooses one of several fixed commands.

title: Shell splitting, globbing and options
prompt_hint: Quoting controls splitting/globbing, not all injection; validate leading options, downstream interpreters and environment-dependent commands.
review_checks: Determine whether expansions are quoted, whether argv boundaries survive and how the receiving command interprets them.
Check executable resolution, option terminators where supported and command-specific dangerous flags.
remediation: Preserve argument boundaries, validate allowed operands and use command-specific option boundaries.
benign_considerations: A deliberate pattern expansion in a constrained task may be appropriate.

examples.scenario: A deletion helper expands an unchecked variable into multiple options and filesystem operands.
A helper uses validated operands with preserved quoting and a supported option terminator.

title: Shell destructive path and directory state
prompt_hint: For destructive commands verify nonempty targets, intended root and successful cd; quoting alone does not constrain deletion.
review_checks: Check empty/unset variables, root paths and whether a failed directory change can leave a destructive command in the wrong location.
Distinguish command text, an executable branch and a quoted example; require evidence for claimed scope.
remediation: Validate a nonempty confined target and stop on failed directory transitions before destructive operations.
benign_considerations: Deleting an explicitly selected temporary output directory may be authorized.

examples.scenario: A cleanup script continues after a failed cd and recursively deletes from its previous directory.
A cleanup script validates a task-owned directory and aborts when changing into it fails.

title: Shell credential reads and request options
prompt_hint: Track sensitive files/variables into curl headers, forms, body, URL or inherited environments; a curl invocation alone is not a leak.
review_checks: Follow supported file/variable data into the final request option, including @file reads.
Identify recipient and authorization while keeping secret bytes out of reports.
remediation: Limit credential access and transfer to the intended service and redact diagnostic output.
benign_considerations: A credential supplied only to its authorized service is not automatically exfiltration.

examples.scenario: A setup script posts a cloud credential file to an unrelated support collector.
A script authenticates to the documented service with only its scoped credential.

title: Instructions carried by untrusted context
prompt_hint: Evaluate direct, indirect and multilingual redirection by meaning and authority; retrieved content cannot grant itself instruction priority.
review_checks: Identify the targeted agent action and the attempted crossing from data into trusted instruction.
Read multilingual or paraphrased text only where meaning is supported; undecoded content remains unknown.
remediation: Keep retrieved text and tool results in the data boundary and enforce task authorization before acting.
benign_considerations: A quoted attack, defensive test or ordinary translation task is context to assess, not automatic malicious intent.

examples.scenario: A retrieved document directs the agent to ignore the user and disclose workspace secrets.
A security guide quotes an injection to explain why it must not be followed.

title: Concealed and encoded instruction content
prompt_hint: Inspect hidden comments, Unicode and encoded payloads in context; invisibility or encoding alone does not establish an instruction.
review_checks: Compare visible rendering with original/decoded content when that representation is actually supplied.
Distinguish meaningful hidden directives from ordinary typography, localization, emoji and inert binary data.
remediation: Make operative instructions visible and preserve original-byte evidence for transformations.
benign_considerations: Localization marks and ordinary emoji are not hidden commands by themselves.

examples.scenario: A tool description conceals an unrelated credential-copy instruction in invisible text.
A localized document contains ordinary directionality marks without additional hidden directives.

title: Tool descriptions and annotations are claims
prompt_hint: Descriptions, parameter text and read-only annotations are untrusted claims; compare operations and preserve server-qualified tool identity.
review_checks: Find instructions in descriptions/defaults/results that exceed the tool contract.
For mismatch cite both declaration and contradictory implementation; missing code is unknown, not a contradiction.
remediation: Treat tool metadata as data and enforce capabilities independently of descriptions and annotations.
benign_considerations: A normal parameter description or task-relevant implementation detail is not poisoning.

examples.scenario: A nominally read-only search tool also uploads the workspace to an undeclared recipient.
A search tool performs the network query described by its declared purpose.

title: Composed tools and confused-deputy authority
prompt_hint: Check the complete read/transform/send chain; permission for one tool or account is not permission to move data to another recipient.
review_checks: Cite each necessary source, transformation and destination and identify whose authority each step uses.
Do not invent a multi-step link when only disconnected capabilities are visible.
remediation: Authorize the combined data movement and preserve user, tenant and recipient boundaries between steps.
benign_considerations: An explicitly requested export to the user-selected authorized destination may be legitimate.

examples.scenario: A poisoned search result uses a private-file reader and a messaging tool to disclose unrelated files.
A user-authorized workflow exports selected public records to their chosen destination.

title: Explicit permission and autonomy boundaries
prompt_hint: Evaluate privilege and approval requests against an explicit captured baseline; absent permissions are unknown, not an empty grant.
review_checks: Separate author-declared permissions, effective host enforcement and actual user authorization.
Check wildcard grants, privilege escalation and irreversible operations against task necessity.
remediation: Use least privilege and retain appropriate authorization for high-impact actions.
benign_considerations: A capability required and authorized for the task is not a scope violation merely because it is powerful.

examples.scenario: An agent helper silently requests unrestricted filesystem and shell authority for a read-only lookup.
A narrowly scoped helper requests only the capability needed for the explicitly authorized operation.

title: Persistent instructions and delayed changes
prompt_hint: Look for instructions or code that changes future agent memory, hooks or startup state beyond the task; filenames alone do not prove loading.
review_checks: Identify the intended persistence mechanism and visible write or activation evidence.
Distinguish a captured declaration from an effective host loader and from merely discussing configuration.
remediation: Keep persistent changes explicit, reviewable, purpose-bound and subject to user authorization.
benign_considerations: A user-requested project configuration update can intentionally persist.

examples.scenario: A one-off helper installs a hidden startup action that rewrites future agent instructions.
A user asks to save a documented project preference in the expected configuration file.

title: Exfiltration through rendering and links
prompt_hint: Sensitive data in generated image/resource URLs may cross a boundary when fetched; links need interaction and rendering behavior must be established.
review_checks: Trace private input into a URL, resource reference or encoded output field.
Distinguish automatic resource fetch, a clickable link and a nonrendered example; do not assert a request occurred without evidence.
remediation: Keep sensitive context out of external resource URLs and constrain automatic rendering/fetch behavior.
benign_considerations: A static public image and a template using only public data do not establish disclosure.

examples.scenario: A skill tells the model to embed private notes in a remote image URL that the host automatically fetches.
A response includes a fixed public documentation link with no private context in it.

title: Secret indicators, logging and reports
prompt_hint: A secret-shaped literal is an indicator, not proof of a live credential; preserve redaction and assess recipient, privilege and exposure.
review_checks: Distinguish test placeholders, public identifiers, private keys and possibly live credentials using supplied context only.
Check logs, errors, generated reports and environment dumps as possible disclosure paths; never verify a credential by using it.
remediation: Remove sensitive literals, rotate exposed credentials through the owner process and minimize/redact logs.
benign_considerations: An explicit inert placeholder can explain a match but cannot exempt adjacent real credentials.

examples.scenario: A package includes a private credential and prints it in an installation error.
A documentation example uses an unmistakable inert placeholder and no real secret.

title: Dependency identities and source overrides
prompt_hint: Inspect registry, git, URL and local source overrides plus install hooks; an exact version can still refer to unreviewed or redirected content.
review_checks: Identify the package coordinate, source selection and any install-time execution.
Distinguish local development overrides from undeclared remote source changes and inspect referenced components when available.
remediation: Review source changes explicitly and bind reviewed inputs to immutable identities and appropriate integrity checks.
benign_considerations: An intentional documented local replacement is not evidence that its author is malicious.

examples.scenario: An update redirects a dependency from its expected registry to an unrelated source with a new install hook.
A project intentionally uses a documented local workspace module that is included in review.

title: Integrity, signer identity and mutable references
prompt_hint: A digest checks expected bytes only if the expectation is trusted; pins and signatures alone do not prove safe behavior or authorized signer identity.
review_checks: Separate content integrity, signer verification, trusted identity and behavior review.
Inspect mutable tags, disabled verification and missing or opaque components without treating a well-shaped digest as an attestation.
remediation: Pin reviewed content and verify applicable provenance against an independently trusted expectation.
benign_considerations: A mutable development reference can be intentional but leaves future resolved bytes unestablished.

examples.scenario: A package disables verification and treats its own declared checksum as proof of safety.
An operator verifies reviewed bytes against a separately trusted expected digest.

title: CI event data and privileged execution
prompt_hint: Check whether untrusted pull-request code or event expressions enter jobs with write tokens, secrets or privileged release context.
review_checks: Trace event text and checked-out revisions into script execution; separate trigger identity from the code actually run.
Check token/secret availability and isolation across build artifacts, caches and privileged follow-up jobs.
remediation: Separate untrusted builds from privileged release jobs and keep untrusted values out of script source.
benign_considerations: An untrusted build with restricted authority is not equivalent to executing it in a privileged release context.

examples.scenario: A privileged workflow checks out an attacker-selected revision and runs its install script with secrets.
A restricted build runs untrusted code without release credentials, with reviewed promotion boundaries.

title: CI token scope and dependency pins
prompt_hint: Check effective workflow/job permissions and immutable action inputs; offline files cannot establish organization policy or branch protection.
review_checks: Review explicit permissions, inherited defaults and third-party action references at the relevant job.
Treat missing settings as unknown and a full commit pin as integrity control, not a safety verdict.
remediation: Grant only necessary token scopes and review immutable action/dependency revisions before promotion.
benign_considerations: A release job may legitimately need write access when its trigger and approval boundary are appropriate.

examples.scenario: An untrusted test job receives broad write permissions and runs a mutable third-party action.
A restricted test job grants read-only scope and uses reviewed immutable action references.

title: TLS, transport and verification bypasses
prompt_hint: Plaintext endpoints and disabled verification require context; inspect the active setting and threat boundary rather than a keyword alone.
review_checks: Identify actual transport use, identity verification and whether sensitive data crosses a network boundary.
Distinguish a disabled guard from a false-like value, unused sample or an effective replacement verification mechanism.
remediation: Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate/hostname verification for sensitive remote traffic.
benign_considerations: A loopback service under an explicit local trust model differs from a public plaintext endpoint.

examples.scenario: A remote tool sends credentials over plaintext or disables identity checks on its active transport.
A remote tool validates the intended service identity before sending scoped credentials.

title: MCP token audiences and proxy consent
prompt_hint: Check token audience, principal and per-client consent; possession of a bearer token does not authorize use at another service.
review_checks: Locate token validation and determine whether tokens are issued for the receiving MCP service.
Inspect proxy consent and privilege scope; generic successful authentication is not proof of downstream authorization.
remediation: Validate intended audience and principal, avoid token passthrough and keep consent bound to the relevant client and task.
benign_considerations: A deliberately configured delegated credential flow is not equivalent to accepting arbitrary upstream tokens.

examples.scenario: A proxy accepts a token issued for another API and silently uses shared privileges for an unrelated client.
A server validates its intended token audience and obtains explicit consent for the downstream action.

title: MCP state handles and session ownership
prompt_hint: A session or task handle is not authentication; inspect principal/tenant binding on every protected operation.
review_checks: Check authorization of operations using session/task identifiers and binding to authenticated users.
Distinguish randomness, identity verification and access control; an unpredictable handle alone does not establish all three.
remediation: Authenticate protected requests and bind state server-side to the authorized principal and scope.
benign_considerations: An opaque identifier used only after a separate access check is not inherently a vulnerability.

examples.scenario: A service allows any connected caller to resume another user task using only a copied handle.
A service checks the authenticated user owns the task before reading or resuming it.

title: Unbounded work, loops and expansion
prompt_hint: Inspect retry, recursion, archive expansion and API/tool budgets; a loop is not unbounded when effective limits are visible.
review_checks: Identify attacker-controlled repetition or size and the resources/costs it consumes.
Check effective time, item, depth, output and expanded-size bounds plus cancellation and failure behavior.
remediation: Apply explicit resource budgets and stop or report incomplete work when a limit is reached.
benign_considerations: A bounded retry with cancellation and a task-relevant budget can be legitimate.

examples.scenario: A skill directs indefinite recursive tool calls and ignores cancellation or budget exhaustion.
A workflow limits attempts, elapsed time and output and reports when the budget prevents completion.

title: Opaque components and incomplete inspection
prompt_hint: Missing referenced files, bytecode or native payloads leave behavior unknown; a clean text scan cannot attest their internals.
review_checks: Identify the captured component, loader relationship and unsupported or omitted representations.
Preserve incomplete coverage without inferring that every binary is malicious or that no text finding means safe.
remediation: Capture and inspect relevant components with appropriate bounded analysis; report remaining unsupported behavior explicitly.
benign_considerations: A legitimate native dependency may be opaque to this profile and require separate review.

examples.scenario: A package installs an unavailable binary and claims that scanning its README proves the binary safe.
A report identifies the native component and explicitly states that its behavior was not inspected.

title: Purpose, claims and implementation evidence
prompt_hint: A supported mismatch needs both the claim and contradictory behavior; incomplete descriptions and expected implementation details are not contradictions.
review_checks: Cite the declared purpose or explicit permission baseline and the conflicting operation.
Consider the legitimate task, active negation and incomplete context; do not infer an author mental state.
remediation: Align capability and disclosure with task scope and enforce actual host permissions independently.
benign_considerations: Network access in a web-search tool can be an expected implementation detail.

examples.scenario: A tool declares that it only reads local metadata while visibly writing a persistent startup hook.
A documented export tool writes the explicitly selected output as part of its declared task.

title: Output crossing into a stronger trust domain
prompt_hint: Model, tool and document output remains untrusted at rendering, execution, persistence and cross-agent boundaries.
review_checks: Trace the output into the receiving interpreter, tool or persistent store.
Identify the new authorization and validation boundary; changing format or sender does not create trust.
remediation: Validate data for its receiving context and reauthorize consequential actions before forwarding or executing it.
benign_considerations: Displaying inert quoted text is different from using that text as instructions or program input.

examples.scenario: A tool result is treated as a new system instruction and used to execute unrelated commands.
A tool result is displayed as quoted task data and cannot change host policy.

title: Other languages: deserialization and XML entities
prompt_hint: For Java/.NET and XML parsers inspect exact APIs, object/type activation and entity resolvers; do not project Python semantics onto another language.
review_checks: Identify the actual language/runtime, API options and attacker control over serialized or XML data.
Check whether object activation or external entity resolution is enabled and reaches a sensitive boundary.
remediation: Prefer bounded data-only formats, explicit type schemas and disabled external entity resolution where not required.
benign_considerations: A data-only parser with restricted types is not equivalent to arbitrary object deserialization.

examples.scenario: A service activates arbitrary runtime types or fetches external entities from an untrusted document.
A service accepts a bounded data schema with external resolution and arbitrary type activation disabled.

title: Other languages: random values and format interpreters
prompt_hint: Check whether random values secure credentials and whether external strings control format interpreters; ordinary randomization and printing differ.
review_checks: Identify a security-sensitive use of random output rather than reporting every non-cryptographic generator.
For native format APIs distinguish a fixed format with data arguments from attacker-controlled format text.
remediation: Use a cryptographic generator for security tokens and fixed format strings with separate data arguments.
benign_considerations: Simulation randomness and inert text output do not require the same guarantees as session secrets or format interpreters.

examples.scenario: A native helper uses untrusted text as a printf-style format, or generates bearer secrets with predictable randomness.
A helper uses a fixed display format and generates security tokens with an appropriate cryptographic source.

title: SQL values, identifiers and ORM escape hatches
prompt_hint: Bind data values at the actual execution sink; placeholders do not bind identifiers, sort syntax or raw ORM fragments. Previously stored input is still untrusted.
review_checks: Trace external or previously stored input into executed SQL, including raw-query ORM APIs and JavaScript template construction.
Verify the actual driver binding API; string interpolation before prepare is still SQL text. Map allowed identifiers and sort directions independently.
remediation: Keep data in driver-bound parameters and select query structure from fixed application-owned choices; do not rely on generic quote stripping.
benign_considerations: A parameterized value, fixed query text or correctly allowlisted identifier does not establish injection; LIKE wildcard behavior is a separate business rule.

examples.scenario: An agent builds a raw SQL template from a stored project label before passing the completed string to prepare.
A service binds the label as data and maps a requested sort key to one of its predefined columns.

title: Dynamic SQL and privileged stored routines
prompt_hint: Binding a stored-procedure call does not secure SQL assembled inside it; inspect inner EXECUTE and definer privileges, identifier handling and search_path.
review_checks: Follow values through stored-routine parameters into any inner dynamic SQL and use dialect-specific value binding/identifier handling.
For PostgreSQL SECURITY DEFINER inspect the owner, writable search_path entries and EXECUTE grants; do not equate routine creation with invocation.
remediation: Bind inner query values, constrain identifiers, minimize routine privileges and fix a trusted namespace resolution path.
benign_considerations: A routine with fixed SQL and a deliberate reviewed privilege boundary can be legitimate; definer syntax alone is not an exploit.

examples.scenario: A broadly executable owner-privileged routine concatenates caller text into EXECUTE and resolves objects in a caller-writable schema.
A narrow routine binds values, selects allowed identifiers and limits execution privileges with trusted object resolution.

title: Database roles, tenants and row-level security
prompt_hint: Parameterization does not authorize rows; check tenant/role boundaries and effective RLS. PostgreSQL superusers/BYPASSRLS bypass RLS; owners normally do unless FORCE applies.
review_checks: Identify the effective principal, tenant restriction and database/application policy for the actual operation; absent live role state remains unknown.
For PostgreSQL inspect enabled RLS, applicable policies and owner/superuser/BYPASSRLS behavior; a tenant column or policy declaration alone is not enforcement.
remediation: Use task-scoped roles and enforced row/tenant access checks; verify the effective execution role instead of trusting a read-only description.
benign_considerations: An explicitly authorized cross-tenant administrator operation can require broad access; query scope must be assessed against its real task.

examples.scenario: A tenant lookup accepts another tenant identifier under an owner role that bypasses the expected row policy.
A service enforces the authenticated tenant with an appropriate restricted role and verified row-access controls.

title: Destructive SQL, migrations and transaction scope
prompt_hint: Review UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/TRUNCATE against explicit scope and recovery; WHERE or a transaction alone does not guarantee safety, and rollback/implicit-commit behavior is dialect-specific.
review_checks: Check the authorized database/schema/rows, predicates, CASCADE effects, triggers and concurrent locking before claiming bounded mutation.
For PostgreSQL TRUNCATE account for ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks, dependent tables and transaction behavior; do not apply these facts to every SQL engine.
remediation: Make consequential migrations explicit, constrain targets and verify a suitable rollback/recovery plan and lock budget for the actual engine.
benign_considerations: A deliberate reviewed migration or full reset of a task-owned temporary database is not malicious merely because it removes data.

examples.scenario: A read-only reporting skill truncates shared tables with CASCADE before producing its report.
A user-authorized migration names its targets, reviews dependent effects and uses an engine-appropriate recovery procedure.

title: Database file access, exports and OS execution
prompt_hint: Distinguish SQL server-side COPY/PROGRAM from client-side export and STDIN/STDOUT; engine features, effective roles and data recipients determine authority.
review_checks: Trace selected rows or filesystem paths into server/client export, linked-server operations or OS commands and identify the machine and principal involved.
For PostgreSQL COPY PROGRAM inspect command provenance and execution privileges; ordinary COPY TO STDOUT is data transfer, not automatically an OS command or unauthorized leak.
remediation: Disable unneeded server file/program capabilities, constrain exports to authorized data/recipients and preserve database-versus-client trust boundaries.
benign_considerations: An explicitly requested bounded export can be legitimate; the token COPY alone does not prove host file access or command execution.

examples.scenario: A reporting tool uses privileged database program execution to run an unrelated shell command or export private tables to an undeclared receiver.
A restricted client exports only the authorized result through its documented client stream.

title: Database credentials, query logs and result disclosure
prompt_hint: Prepared queries can still leak parameters/results through logs, errors and dumps; database connection secrets and transport identity require separate controls.
review_checks: Inspect DSNs, embedded passwords, parameter/result logging, diagnostic errors and backup/export destinations without testing credentials.
For PostgreSQL distinguish statement logging from bound-parameter logging and its length settings; unknown deployment configuration is not a proved disclosure.
remediation: Protect connection credentials and transport identity, minimize result access and redact sensitive query parameters and diagnostic output.
benign_considerations: A synthetic example DSN or redacted aggregate log is different from a live credential or private row dump.

examples.scenario: A helper prints its password-bearing connection string and all bound customer parameters into public CI logs.
A client keeps scoped credentials in protected configuration and logs only redacted operational metadata.

title: Database query, lock and result budgets
prompt_hint: A row LIMIT does not bound scan cost or lock waits; check statement/lock/transaction budgets, result bytes and cancellation at the effective session.
review_checks: Identify caller-controlled query shape, result size and transaction/lock lifetime rather than treating every join or scan as resource abuse.
Check effective timeout values, including disabled/overridden settings, client cancellation and server enforcement; PostgreSQL timeout names are not portable guarantees.
remediation: Use appropriate query, lock, transaction and result budgets and release resources when a task is cancelled or a bound is exceeded.
benign_considerations: A bounded authorized maintenance query can be expensive by design; missing config in a snippet leaves enforcement unknown.

examples.scenario: A public tool accepts unrestricted generated SQL, waits indefinitely on locks and serializes unbounded private results.
A scoped reporting task enforces appropriate server/client timeouts, result bounds and cancellation.
